verdict.rationale: Teller documents a transactions API that exposes an account's ledger transactions, and its list endpoint supports pagination controls, so the core retrieval and pagination parts are covered. However, no history depth is documented. There is also no incremental "fetch only what changed" sync pattern; webhooks only signal that enrollment or financial data changed and are not a delta-fetch mechanism. Missing for 10: documented history depth, an incremental/delta sync pattern for transactions, detailed pagination semantics, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can pull transaction history for a connected account through the API — paginated, with documented history depth and a sync pattern for fetching only what changed

citations.quote: The transactions API exposes the ledger transactions of a financial account.
the transactions list endpoint supports pagination controls.
